meta.title: UAE map data for the NCM 20th-anniversary film
meta.rings: Every polygon is one outer ring, listed without repeating the first point (close it when drawing). No holes are needed: Madha (Oman) is a gap between the Sharjah and Fujairah polygons, and Nahwa is its own Sharjah polygon inside that gap.
meta.simplification: 1) Morphological opening of the whole land mass by 200 m (erode, then dilate), which removes land narrower than 400 m: causeways, breakwaters, the palm islands' fronds, sand spits. 2) Islets under 5.0 km2 dropped (101 of them) unless named. 3) Douglas-Peucker (topology-preserving) in x = lon*cos(24.4 deg), y = lat, tolerance 0.004 deg (about 445 m; islands use a finer tolerance scaled to their size), run once per shared chain so neighbouring emirates, and the UAE and its neighbours, keep identical borders. 4) Rounded to 4 decimals; 0 rounding knot(s) untied and 1 island overlap(s) cut, see validation.

projection.formula: x = (lon - bbox.lonMin) * kx * s ; y = (bbox.latMax - lat) * s ; kx = cos(24.4 deg)
projection.js: const KX = Math.cos(24.4 * Math.PI / 180); function fit(b, W, H, pad) { const s = Math.min((W - 2 * pad) / ((b[2] - b[0]) * KX), (H - 2 * pad) / (b[3] - b[1])); const ox = (W - (b[2] - b[0]) * KX * s) / 2, oy = (H - (b[3] - b[1]) * s) / 2; return ([lon, lat]) => [ox + (lon - b[0]) * KX * s, oy + (b[3] - lat) * s]; }

bbox.note: All seven emirates including the three islands (Greater Tunb sets latMax).

projection.scale_note: At kx the map is true to scale in both axes at 24.4 N; 1 deg latitude is about 110.8 km.

arcs.note: The same outline cut into drawable strokes, so a line can "ink itself" in order. type coast = shoreline (island rings are closed); land_border = with Oman (OMN) or Saudi Arabia (SAU); emirate_border = between two emirates (each drawn once).

context.note: Faint neighbours only, clipped to the frame: Oman (with Musandam and Madha), Saudi Arabia, Qatar. Iran and its islands such as Sirri are left out on purpose. Borders with the UAE are the very same simplified chains as the UAE side, so there are no slivers. Draw them lighter than the UAE and do not label them unless the protocol office asks.
context.holes_note: holes[] are cut-outs (fill with evenodd); the only one is Nahwa inside Omani Madha, which the Sharjah polygon then fills.

points.note: OurAirports gives this latitude to only 2 decimals (about 1 km); the point still falls on Dalma Island. Fine for a map mark, not for a close-up.
Summit. The mountain lies on the UAE-Oman border; the summit point falls inside the Abu Dhabi polygon. NCM also has a Jabal Hafeet station (41227) at 24.0567 N, 55.7753 E (zenodo_ncm_stations).

Marker placed on the UAE side: the highest DEM cell inside the Ras Al Khaimah polygon, about 270 m west of the summit, matching Wikipedia's "high point west of this peak". The summit itself (25.95306 N, 56.18417 E) is on the Omani side, about 140 m outside the Ras Al Khaimah polygon. At film scale (on a 1920x1080 frame showing the whole country, 1 px is about 400 m) the two are the same point. Do not print an elevation from this file.

points.fact: 254.8 mm in less than 24 hours on 16 April 2024 (NCM; worded as on the NCM at Twenty page, source 28)
points.note: Two sources give the same position; they differ on the station height (406 m vs 433 m), so do not print a height.

radar_note.published_by_ncm: NCM's own radar-network page (ncm.gov.ae/maps-radars/uae-radars-network) could not be reached from this environment (ncm.gov.ae is blocked here). NCM has named the radar towns (Al Bayan, 28 Nov 2020) but not their coordinates.
radar_note.coordinates_from: WMO Radar Database records owned by NCM (self-reported, not WMO-verified).
radar_note.incomplete: The WRD crawl was cut off. Three UAE records were not seen: 0-21010-0-188 "Muzaira Radar" (C-band, 2016; Mezaira'a is one of the towns NCM names), 0-21010-0-657 "Mobile-X" (X-band, 2016) and 0-21010-0-866 (name unknown). So the list of operational radars here may be short by one or more.
radar_note.closed_note: Closed or removed radars, kept out of points[] so they are not drawn by accident. The Al Sila mobile record (0-21010-0-863) plots about 4.5 km outside the UAE outline, so its WRD position is approximate.
radar_note.on_screen_rule: Show only radars with status 'Operational', as unlabelled marks, or not at all. Do not show a radar count from this file; the page's sourced figure is "9 weather radars (2021)" (source 24), and it includes the mobile radars.

islands: Abu Musa is drawn as part of Sharjah, and Greater Tunb and Lesser Tunb as part of Ras Al Khaimah, per the UAE position. The source file used here (geoBoundaries ARE, from OpenStreetMap) leaves them out; their outlines come from Natural Earth (public domain), with Lesser Tunb as a true-size disc at its gazetteer position. No other country's administrative file is used for any UAE territory. The geoBoundaries ADM0 outlines of Oman, Saudi Arabia and Qatar (ODbL) draw only those countries' own faint context shapes, and their borders with the UAE are cut from the UAE's own vertices. The FGIC General Map geometry replaces all of it before lock.
Sir Abu Nu'ayr is moved from Abu Dhabi to Sharjah. The OpenStreetMap-based file has it in Abu Dhabi, but the island belongs to the Emirate of Sharjah (wiki_sir_bu_nair).
oman: Musandam (Oman) is not part of the UAE and is absent from the UAE polygons, so Ras Al Khaimah ends at the Oman border and the tip of the peninsula shows as a gap. It is present, faint, in the context layer.
Madha (Oman) is a gap between Sharjah (Khor Fakkan) and Fujairah; Nahwa (Sharjah, UAE) is its own polygon inside that gap.
protocol.sea_names: If seas are labelled, use the names NCM uses in its own forecasts: "Arabian Gulf" / الخليج العربي (never "Persian Gulf") and "Oman Sea" / بحر عُمان (ncm_bulletin).
protocol.saudi_border: The UAE-Saudi line is the OpenStreetMap version of the 1974 agreement line. The file does not judge it. Before the ceremony, get the outline signed off against an official federal UAE map.
protocol.no_maritime: No maritime limits, EEZ or median lines are drawn.
log: Moved Sir Abu Nu'ayr (Sir Bu Nair) from Abu Dhabi to Sharjah: the OpenStreetMap-based file puts it in Abu Dhabi; the island belongs to the Emirate of Sharjah.
Added Abu Musa (11.8 km2) to Sharjah, per the UAE position; the outline is the Natural Earth 1:10m outline.
Added Greater Tunb (10.5 km2) to Ras Al Khaimah, per the UAE position; the outline is the Natural Earth 1:10m outline.
Added Lesser Tunb (1.9 km2) to Ras Al Khaimah, per the UAE position; the outline is a 2 km2 disc at its gazetteer position (26 14 N, 55 08 E).
Generalised the coast with a 200 m morphological opening (removes causeways, breakwaters, palm fronds and islets narrower than 400 m) before simplification.
Removed 4 zero-area slivers (< 0.05 km2) where the UAE and neighbour source files do not quite meet.

validation.overlap_note: Anything listed here is a sub-metre rounding sliver along a shared border (area in square metres), invisible at film scale.
